name: Silent Lineup

scoring.report_note: Report group-level deltas only. Never rank individuals — the lineup measures the group's coordination habits, not charisma.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for the Silent Lineup leadership exercise. Scores at group level: how did initiative, legibility, distributed permission and follower choice change across the two lineups?

instructions.pre: Before the first lineup. Each participant answers alone, about their own last week at work — not about the exercise.
instructions.post: Immediately after the debrief. Same items, now answered about both lineups, as a group.

items.pre_text: In groups without an appointed leader, I move first.
items.post_text: In the lineups, I (or several of us) moved first without being asked.

items.pre_text: I make my status and needs visible without being asked.
items.post_text: We invented a legible code (finger-months) instead of vague gestures.

items.pre_text: I wait for someone else to unstick a stalled group.
items.post_text: When the line jammed, we waited for someone else to fix it.

items.pre_text: When someone makes a sensible first move, I back it quickly.
items.post_text: The first movers got backed quickly — early followers made it a team.

items.pre_text: I notice when someone is left at the edges of a group.
items.post_text: Someone checked the edges — the January end needed help.

items.pre_text: My team coordinates well even when talking is not possible.
items.post_text: Two lineups, two systems — the group coordinated both times, wordlessly.

report.title: Silent Lineup — group coordination delta
sections: Both lineups: first movers, codes invented, jams and unjamming
One suggested coordination move per group, derived from the largest positive delta
